I did not run commands or inspect files outside the supplied diff, per instruction.","findings":[{"severity":"medium","title":"Plugin manifest records new cache/version paths while retaining old git commit SHAs","body":"Multiple `.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` entries move `installPath` and `version` from `167b871c3223` to `793057a62c58`, but leave `gitCommitSha` at older, plugin-specific SHAs such as `70d57685...`, `4e5dc953...`, `ee652201...`, and `3007c178...`. That makes the manifest internally contradictory: consumers cannot tell whether the installed plugin content is from `793057a62c58` or the retained `gitCommitSha`. For this repo, plugin provenance is an attack surface because these paths point at executable/plugin content under `.claude/plugins/cache`; stale SHAs can break auditability, rollback, update detection, and any gate that trusts `gitCommitSha` as the source revision.","file":".claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json","line_start":76,"line_end":81,"confidence":0.86,"recommendation":"Regenerate or patch the manifest so `version`, `installPath`, and `gitCommitSha` refer to the same upstream revision for every updated plugin entry, or document and encode the distinction if `version` is intentionally a separate marketplace/cache revision."}],"next_steps":["Verify all entries changed from `167b871c3223` to `793057a62c58` have matching source revision metadata.","Check the added `docs/install-provenance.md` block documents the same revision model used by the manifest."]}
